newsitem.title: UK: Brent Walker moves closer to pub sale.
newsitem.headline: Brent Walker moves closer to pub sale.

text.p: Debt-laden leisure group Brent Walker Plc moved closer to a sale of its pub chain Pubmaster on Friday when it announced the selection of a preferred bidder.

The company refused to name the chosen candidate, but market speculation immediately centered on Pubmaster's former chief executive John Brackenbury in cooperation with venture capital specialist NatWest Ventures.
The announcement ends recent rumours that the sale of the chain was in trouble. Brent Walker said negotiations about the disposal were continuing and further details would be announced in due course.
One analyst who asked not to be named said estimates that the chain could fetch 200 million pounds ($313.1 million) were optimistic.
"I think that if Pubmaster get between 150 million and 165 million pounds they are doing very well," he said.
He added that established pub chains seem not to have been interested in Pubmaster "because of the quality of these pubs" and the price being asked.
Brent Walker, which is being sued by its founder George Walker over an alleged unpaid debt, is also trying to sell its other main business, the betting shop chain William Hill.
William Hill has been on the market since 1991 with a price tag of around 500 million stg.

On Monday arbitrators ruled that Brent Walker had paid 117.5 million pounds too much for William Hill and bingo-hall operator Mecca when it acquired the chain from Grand Metroplitan Plc in December 1989.
